official_measurement_examples: forestry EIA covers afforestation deforestation forest roads and forestry quarries
Stage 1 asks Forestry Commission whether significant environmental effects are likely
projects likely to have significant effects require Forestry Commission Stage 2 Consent before proceeding
each distinct forestry project can require its own EIA application
woodland creation grant workflows can provide information relevant to Stage 1 but are not automatically consent
planning EIA and forestry EIA are separate regulatory routes
felling licence and forestry EIA consent are separate controls
Forestry EIA status does not establish ownership planning permission or final development yield
core_rules: forestry EIA is distinct from planning EIA
Stage1 opinion is not Stage2 consent
Stage2 consent is not planning permission
planning permission is not forestry EIA consent
felling licence is not forestry EIA consent
forest road and quarry remain distinct projects
threshold/exemption context must retain sensitive-area rules
grant approval is not EIA consent proof
historic-environment checks do not replace archaeology consents
EIA status does not establish ownership
EIA status does not establish access rights
Forestry Commission map is not cadastral title map
consent does not calculate development yield
no parcel forestry clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official Forestry Commission, GOV.UK, forestry EIA regulations and 2025-2026 guidance checked 2026-07-26. Stage1/Stage2/project-type/felling/planning separation retained; no parcel promotion.
